resolutions.protocol_amendment: Stage 1 amendment (C0F0): (a) C's construct is LIFETIME ever-in-union by end of reproductive life (never-partnered complement at 45-49); the 25-39 partnership stock is demoted to a trend/ordering witness for C dynamics only. (b) (C0, RV0) are derived JOINTLY from cohort-MATCHED pairs {p0(cohort k), ever-in-union(cohort k)} - never chain values from different cohort vintages (the Israel -0.032 'violation' is purely a 1947-67-vs-1971-76 vintage clash). (c) The feasibility constraint C0 >= 1-p0 is checked explicitly per region before RV0 = 1-(1-p0)/C0 is computed, with the delivered margins as the acceptance record; Italy/Poland/Israel margins are thin (<= +0.03 low end) and must carry their uncertainty into RV0's error band. (d) Regions with material non-marital fertility (IL, and to a lesser degree PL/FR/USA) get a stated ~1-2pp leak term: mothers are not a strict subset of the ever-partnered, so RV0 there is a lower bound. (e) Korea's affine endpoint moves from 0.52 (a 25-39 stock) to ~0.85 (cohort-matched lifetime ever-married at 40), and Israel's from 0.97 to ~0.89-0.92 - the current hand-set endpoints mix the two constructs the critic identified. Stage 0 amendment (C0F4): Poland's p0 is recorded as the bracket 0.10-0.20 (late-window central 0.15-0.195, HFD upper bound carrying its documented emigration overestimation), sourced as no-census-possible: NSP 2021 has no children-ever-born question, so 'read the GUS census table' is permanently unsatisfiable and the GUS-preference convention falls back to HFD-register + survey triangulation; 'Poland UP' for C0 stands (0.82 -> ~0.90-0.92) but any statement that C0[PL] MUST rise to >= 0.897 is struck.

resolutions.summary: C0F5 resolved: Korea HAS a national ideal-zero instrument directly comparable to the European personal-ideal question - the KIHASA Family and Fertility Survey (가족과 출산 조사, successor of the National Fertility Survey), ages 19-49, N~14,000 per wave. Table 10-6 of the 2024 report gives the full distribution: ideal-zero = 0.0% in 2021 and 0.2% in 2024 (married 0.2 / unmarried 0.2; two-child ideal 59.2%). Under the consistent IDEAL construct Korea reads at 0.002, i.e. BELOW every European region (Germany 0.075) and two orders of magnitude below the KPPIF 0.426 intention share - the Nhi=0.42 'confirmation' is definitively an instrument artifact, no region occupies the high well, and even the Wave-1 ordering claim (Korea >> Germany) is wrong on the ideal construct. C1F5 resolved: a childfree panel was built from repeated same-instrument waves - EB intended-zero 2001/2006/2011 (Miettinen & Szalma 2014 Table 1, read at source) for France/Germany/Italy (3 points, 10 years - rate estimable) and Poland (2 points), extended by FReDA 2024/25 (Germany 18-29: 16%), CBOS 2017/2022 (Poland childless women 22%→42%), Pew 2018/2021/2023 (USA non-parents 37→44→47%), JNFS 2002-2021 never-married desired-children means (Japan, 5 points/19 years), KOSIS Social Survey child-necessity norm 2018-2024 (Korea, 4 points), and Gallup/KIHASA ideal means. The panel's core lesson for aN/thN: IDEAL-side series are flat everywhere they meet the bar (EU intended-zero drifts <1pp/decade 2001-2011 outside the German 2001 composition spike; German ideal stuck at 2.2 while TFR fell 1.58→1.35; Gallup zero stuck at 2%), while fast drift appears only in INTENTION instruments post-2015 (Korea, US, Poland) - so the stiff-well/no-tipping regime is what the ideal data support, and any moving norm state must be bound to the intended-childlessness construct explicitly.
resolutions.protocol_amendment: NORM0/E41 Stage-0 amendment: (1) Adopt option A strictly - N is an ordering-only latent index; DELETE the 'Korea 0.426 sits exactly on Nhi=0.42' sentence from the calibration narrative and from targets[4].model_mapping; record Korea ideal-zero = 0.000 (2021) / 0.002 (2024) from KIHASA Table 10-6 as the consistent-construct value. Under the ideal-zero construct no region is within an order of magnitude of Nhi=0.42 (max: Germany 0.075), so option B (well relocation pinned by Korea) is rejected, not deferred. (2) The cross-instrument ordering for option A's latent index must be built per-construct: ideal-zero ordering is Germany(0.075) > Japan(0.056) > Italy(0.035) > USA(0.02) ~ Poland(0.02) > France(0.015) > Korea(0.002) > Israel(null) - Korea moves from top to BOTTOM when the construct is held fixed. (3) aN/thN: constrain with the intended-childlessness panels delivered here; regions meeting the >=3-points/>=10-years bar (France, Germany, Italy on EB 2001-2011; Japan on JNFS 2002-2021) all show flat-to-slow drift, i.e. no observed well-to-well transit in ideals/intentions before 2011 - fit aN as stiff and treat thN as unidentified by ideals; if the model requires a fast-moving norm channel, declare an explicit construct switch of the N observable to intended childlessness (where Korea 2024=0.426, USA 2023=0.47 among non-parents, Poland 2022=0.42 among childless women), and carry the instrument wedge (ideal vs intention spans 0.002-0.526 within Korea in the SAME year) as a formal measurement layer, never as state.

resolutions.protocol_amendment:
E41 addendum - marriageable-men observable family (q channel, resolves C1F0).

(1) Observable. Adopt Wilson's marriageable-men index as the family target: MM_r(t) = SR_r(t) x eM_r(t), where SR = men 25-44 / women 25-44 (UN WPP 2024, on-disk population_by_age1.csv) and eM = prime-age (25-54) male employment rate (Eurostat lfsa_ergan for FR/DE/IT/PL; OECD LFS via FRED LREM25MA*A156N for USA/JP/KR/IL). This is the employed-men-per-woman construct of Wilson (1987) - the same construct behind the E22 citations (Autor et al. China shock; Kearney & Wilson fracking). The age-band mismatch (population stock 25-44 vs employment 25-54) is declared and fixed by convention. calibration_targets.csv gains rows for 2000/2010/2023; values in scratchpad/e41_c1f0_marriageable_men.csv.

(2) Gauge and mapping. q is a latent -1..1 deviation with q(2023) = 0 by construction; the family maps DEVIATIONS ONLY: q_obs_r(t) = alpha_r * ln(MM_r(t)/MM_r(2023)). The scale is pinned by the E22 elasticity epsilon = dlnTFR/dlnMM in [0.2, 0.4] (mid 0.3): a sustained q moves Ceq by gqC*q and TFR is proportional to C, so dlnTFR = gqC*q/C0_r, giving the identification gqC*alpha_r = epsilon*C0_r. ONLY THE PRODUCT gqC*alpha_r IS OBSERVABLE. Option A (recommended, non-structural): keep gqC = 0.9 frozen as code convention and set alpha_r = epsilon*C0_r/0.9 (0.17 Korea .. 0.32 Israel at epsilon = 0.3); alpha_r lives in the mapping table only - no code/PARAMS change, all E30/E22 verdicts untouched. Option B (structural): rescale gqC itself - changes intervention gains, triggers the Stage-5 re-verdict gate and the guard-suite re-baselining of C0F7; not this round.

(3) Backtest hook. Initialize q(2000) = alpha_r * ln(MM_r(2000)/MM_r(2023)) instead of 0. Empirically this is ~0 (|q| <= 0.008) for USA/France/Germany/Italy/Japan/Korea - the MM index is flat 2000-2023 for 6/8 regions, so the q=0 baseline gains observational support - and materially negative only for Poland (-0.048) and Israel (-0.029), whose male employment rose 13.0pp and 4.7pp. Feasibility: at epsilon = 0.3, Poland's MM gain (+0.175 ln) is a +5.3% TFR counter-current against the observed 1.37 -> 1.16 decline; the channel is a lever, not the baseline driver, exactly as E22 framed it.

(4) What stays unobserved (explicit). The E30 scar/intergenerational block keeps ZERO observational contact after this family: wScar = 0.5, wF = 0.6, phi = 0.4, gA = 0.5, the CohortMemory lag window (lagLo = 27, lagHi = 45, childhood = 18) and the SIGMA_CAL q-spread 0.10. fF/fScar are intervention-only forcings, identically zero at baseline, so no 2000-2023 series can constrain their weights. Honest future anchors: intergenerational fertility-transmission correlations (~0.1-0.2 mother-daughter completed fertility) for gA; the lag window is demographically fixed by the reproductive span. All flagged judgment-only in the mapping table.

(5) Caveats carried with the family. (i) Korea's 2023 sex-ratio bulge (25-34 = 1.136) is a WPP population-stock fact; its attribution is left open - the on-disk WPP SRB reads 103-104 for Korea's 1990s births, at odds with registered SRB 112-116, so use the stock, do not narrate the driver. (ii) Israel pre-2012 employment sits on the old CBS LFS design (annual, excl. career soldiers); vintages differ ~1.5pp in 2000 - treat Israel's 2000 MM level as +/-0.02. (iii) Eurostat LFS carries the 2021 IESS break; Poland 2010 differs by vintage (Eurostat 82.5 vs OECD 79.9) - post-census re-weighted Eurostat values adopted for the EU-4. (iv) The cross-region index is employment-only; earnings enter as a USA-only witness (BLS real median weekly earnings, men FT: 372.5 -> 377.75 -> 394.5 in 1982-84 USD, +5.9% over 23 years - the flat-male-earnings signal); INSEE/Destatis publish male MEANS or non-sex-split real indices, no clean public male real MEDIAN series (nulls logged).

resolutions.summary: C1F6 is resolved on three fronts. (1) ANCHOR: fec(tau)=exp(-0.03*(tau-30)) is validated at the model's operating point. All 8 regions' 2023 mean childbearing age sits in 29.9-33.6, and in that 30-35 window the published biological decline is 0.016/yr (Leridon 2004, share achieving a live birth within 4 yr: 91/84/64% at 30/35/40), 0.026/yr (Leridon 2004 within 1 yr: 75/66/44%), and 0.017-0.042/yr (Coale-Trussell natural marital fertility standard); Leridon 1977 childlessness gives 0.016/yr. The 0.03 constant is a defensible central linearization there, but it UNDERSTATES the convex acceleration above ~35 (0.054-0.081/yr Leridon; 0.131/yr Coale-Trussell 37-42) - which matters only if a lever pushes entry age past ~35. The age-30 knee matches te Velde ('decline after 27, steep after 35') and Leridon (fecundability stable into early 30s) as the biological onset - but it is an ENTRY-age threshold. (2) LOCAL FIT: the within-schedule log-linear ASFR decay above 30 (2023, ages 30-44) is 0.19-0.26/yr per region (steepening to 0.41-0.87/yr over 40-49); this is the age-shape gradient (parity-completion + biology), an upper bound NOT directly comparable to fec, which keys off the MEAN not the tail. The alternative 'log(sum ASFR>=30) vs MAC' construction has the WRONG SIGN (+0.10 to +0.21, later timing packs more births above 30), so it cannot anchor a fecundity penalty; the correct anchor is the biological slope in (1). (3) DELTA1: the MAC-MAB1 gap is NOT constant and NOT stationary - 2023 spans 0.46 yr (Korea) to 3.15 yr (Israel). It SHRANK in the deep-postponement collapse countries (Korea 1.23->0.46, Poland 2.86->1.49, Italy ->0.51, Japan ->0.91) as first-birth age caught up to MAC, but stays wide in the one healthy above-replacement basin (Israel ~3.15, early entry + long span) and in the USA (~2.4). Recommendation in protocol_amendment: keep tau=MAC for tempo/quantum/Bongaarts-Feeney this round; register a structural experiment that re-keys the biological terms (fec, gRV childlessness) off entry age = MAC - Delta1_r, because keyed to MAC the 30 knee fires Delta1_r years early - a wash for Korea (0.46) but a spurious biological tax on Israel (3.15, entry 27.7 is BELOW the knee) and the USA.
resolutions.protocol_amendment: STAGE 0 amendment to the C1F6 (Delta1 / fecundity-keying) fork. (a) Keep tau = MAC as the single age observable driving the tempo/quantum dynamics and the Bongaarts-Feeney term (kBF=0.6, pinned by the on-disk WPP MAC series and adjTFR) - unchanged this round, consistent with the synthesis. (b) fec slope: retain 0.03/yr as VALIDATED at the current operating point (all 2023 MAC in 29.9-33.6), citing Leridon 2004 (0.016/yr 30-35 for >=1 child within 4 yr; 0.026/yr within 1 yr) and the Coale-Trussell natural-fertility standard (0.017/yr 27-32, 0.042/yr 32-37). Document the known limitation: the single exponential understates the convex late-30s acceleration (0.05-0.13/yr), so any intervention that drives entry age above ~35 needs a convex fec, not the linear one - flag as a bounded structural experiment, do NOT change the functional form this round. (c) 30 knee: retain, but re-label in code/comment as a biological ENTRY-age threshold (subfecundity onset, te Velde/Leridon), NOT a mean-age threshold. (d) NEW registered structural experiment (next round, not this calibration): re-key the two BIOLOGICAL terms only - fec(.) and the childlessness driver gRV*max(.-30,0) - off an entry-age proxy tau_entry = MAC - Delta1_r (approx MAB1), leaving tempo/quantum on MAC. Rationale: the sterility/subfecundity clock is governed by START age, and Delta1_r is materially non-zero and region-specific. 2023 Delta1_r to use: USA 2.40, France 2.48, Germany 1.67, Italy 0.51, Japan 0.91, Korea 0.46, Poland 1.49, Israel 3.15. Expected effect: negligible for Korea/Italy/Japan (late entry, small gap - biological drag genuine and retained), but removes a spurious biological penalty from Israel (entry 27.7 < 30 knee -> fec approx 1) and the USA (entry 27.5 < knee) - correcting the fact that keyed to MAC all 8 regions currently pay a fecundability tax even where women start young. Because Delta1_r shrank over 2000-2023 in the collapse countries but persists in Israel/USA, the keying choice is a wash exactly where collapse is deepest and decisive exactly in the one healthy basin - which is why it must be resolved as a named structural experiment rather than left as an undocumented default.

E41 protocol amendment (C1F1) - migration wiring.

STAGE 0 ADDITION (definitions). Migration series-of-record = UN WPP 2024 NetMigrations (thousands/yr, all ages, both sexes) and CNMR, on disk in data/raw/unwpp/demographic_indicators.csv (VarID=2), validated this round against the Wave-1 gapfill (80/80 series points exact, 13/13 count claims exact). The Poland-prefers-GUS convention is explicitly NOT extended to migration (GUS counts permanent-residence registrations only, +6.8k in 2023, vs WPP's residence-concept +967.7k Ukrainian wave in 2022). Data caveats recorded: Japan and Korea 2023 NetMigrations are exact carry-forwards of 2022 (175.0k, 87.8k) - WPP assumptions, not measurements; Poland 2022 (CNMR 25.2) is the Ukrainian displacement wave.

BACKTEST STAGE (2000-2023) - observed-migration forcing, zero new fitted parameters. (1) Add "NetMigrations" to coremodel._IND_COLS (coremodel.py:40 - the loader currently drops a column the CSV already carries). (2) At each backtest year t the Leslie step consumes mig_t = NetMigrations[r][t] x RC, where RC is the existing Rogers-Castro profile (coremodel.rogers_castro:236-243, normalized to sum 1, already built at emergent.py:193); leslie_step already accepts mig and splits it 50/50 by sex (coremodel.py:107-129); the three call sites (emergent.py:309/436/609) replace 0.0*self.RC with the year-t observed forcing IN BACKTEST MODE ONLY. Units are consistent end-to-end (WPP thousands on stocks and flows). Nothing is fitted: the forcing is the observed count, RC keeps its canonical unfitted shape, and that shape is a stated limitation (Israel 2022-23 and Germany 2015/2022 waves have non-canonical age profiles). (3) Convention: the year-t flow enters the step advancing the population t to t+1, "added after natural change" per the leslie_step docstring. (4) Sanity tripwire: assert all age bins non-negative after the migration add (worst case on the window, Germany 2006 net -489.1k, removes 13.8k per sex from a ~512k bin - 2.7% - so this is a guard, not a mechanism). (5) What it buys: pop_pct, the dependency ratio, and the dep_pen->S feedback become checkable against observation for the high-migration regions - cumulative 2000-2023 net migration is 10.0% of 2023 population for USA, 8.4% Germany, 8.1% Italy, 4.9% Israel, too large for any pyramid or dependency backtest to ignore. Poland pyramid/dependency pass-fail must be evaluated with 2022-23 excluded (single-shock-year dominance).

## C0F1 - REPLACEMENT FOR STAGE 4 (kBF adjudication on GAP DYNAMICS, never levels)

STAGE 4 - kBF adjudication (gap dynamics). Level-scoring of quantum*fec against published adjTFR is BANNED: by the PB0 identity (emergent.py:196) quantum*fec equals TFR_2023 at the anchor for every kBF, and realized dtau ~ 0 there, so levels are degenerate by construction; the 2023 tempo gap is absorbed into PB0 and stays there. Score instead:
(1) MODEL SIDE: from the frozen Stage-3 backtest (secTau/kTau already refit against the MAC(t) witness so in-window realized dtau spans ~0.09-0.23 yr/yr), take the harness's realized annual tempo change dtau_m(r,t) = tau(r,t) - tau(r,t-1) (post-clip, the E40 convention, emergent.py:287) from the scalar run(); G_model(r,t; kBF) = kBF * dtau_m(r,t).
(2) OBSERVED SIDE: G_obs(r,t) = 1 - TFR_obs(r,t)/adjTFR_obs(r,t) using published Bongaarts-Feeney adjTFR series (HFD tempo-adjusted TFR tables; VID European Demographic Datasheet snapshots; the payload's tempo-adjusted family rows). Window: all backtest region-years 2000-2019 with a published adjTFR value; 2020-2022 excluded; Israel excluded (adjTFR null). A region with only a latest-value adjTFR contributes that single year.
(3) SMOOTHING: both G_model and G_obs are 3-year centered rolling means before differencing (annual dtau and adjTFR are noisy).
(4) STATISTIC: chi2_G(kBF) = sum_{r,t} [G_model(r,t;kBF) - G_obs(r,t)]^2 / sigma_G(r,t)^2 with sigma_G(r,t) = 0.1 * TFR_obs/adjTFR_obs^2 (the protocol's own +-0.1 adjTFR volatility propagated; Korea ~0.071, USA ~0.049 per point), evaluated on the grid kBF in {0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0}.
(5) DECISION: keep kBF = 0.6 unless the grid argmin beats chi2_G(0.6) by more than 4.0 (a 2-sigma move on one effective parameter). If kBF moves, return to Stage 2 (PB_SCALE_ENS refit) exactly once - the loop converges because kBF only touches the tempo factor.
(6) REPORT: the per-region-year (G_model, G_obs, sigma_G) triples and the chi2_G grid go in the experiments log; a systematic residual sign (e.g. Korea G_obs = 0.287 vs max achievable kBF*dtau) is logged as a tempo-mechanism scope finding, not tuned away.

Therefore: MODEL INTEGRATION over the cohort window.
(1) STAGE 1 ITEM (4) IS REWRITTEN: PB0 recomputes automatically via the line-196 identity; compute PB0_check = CFR_b1975 / ((1 - p0_obs) * fec(MAC_cohort)) and REPORT the raw gap per region labelled "period-vs-cohort erosion signal" - expected positive (check > PB0) and largest for USA/Korea. NO acceptance bar in Stage 1; the raw gap is the tempo+erosion signal assigned elsewhere to secPb/secC/kBF, not a composition indictment.
(2) NEW STAGE 3b - epoch-matched composition check (runs after the Stage-3 backtest is frozen): OBSERVED CFR_obs(r) = sum_{a=15}^{48} ASFR_obs(r, year=1975+a, age=a), the b.1975 cohort diagonal computed locally from data/raw/unwpp/fertility_by_age1.csv (fully on disk: age 15 in 1990 through age 48 in 2023); cross-check against the payload CFR family (USA 2.22, France 2.03, Germany 1.58, Italy 1.43, Japan 1.43, Korea 1.59, Poland 1.60, Israel 3.09) with tolerance 0.05 before use.
